title: RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture and Phase 4 acceptance run
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the final acceptance gate.

Build a RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture in tests/fixtures/revengGraph.ts containing tmux_lib at tmux_lib, jfred/external/tmux_lib, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; two occurrences each of claude_plugin_lib and scenarios; nested submodules beneath ordinary directories; and distinct parent chains. Drive a full run against it in tests/revengEndToEnd.test.ts.

Verify in that fixture that a change originating from any repeated occurrence converges everywhere; all child and ancestor suites pass; approval precedes every commit, merge, and push; all occurrence histories consolidate into one operation per logical repository; gitlinks propagate through the correct explicit parents to the root; and every intended local base ends at the expected merge commit. Also verify no semantic commit, push, integration merge, base mutation, or archival occurs before approval, and that only successfully published tasks are archived.

Phase 4 acceptance: the recursive workflow is the production path, completes the RevEng-shaped run without data loss, and archives only tasks whose integration was successfully published.

title: Grouping accepts legacy files as modifiableFiles via the shared accessor, and never groups on readOnlyFiles
userDescription:
[split-task-child] This task is being created by `/split-task` as one of an already-requested set of 6 children — skip the oversized-task assessment regardless of this task's difficulty. This child's `files` field must be exactly this list, in this order, and no other files: `["scripts/taskGroups.ts", "tests/taskGroups.test.ts"]`.

Child 4 of 6 from parent task 58 ("Split task file ownership into modifiableFiles and readOnlyFiles, and make briefs point at files instead of pasting them"). This child owns STEP 4: when a task only has 'files' but not 'modifiableFiles', accept 'files'.

Required behavior:
1. scripts/taskGroups.ts declaredFiles (line 16) currently reads the raw 'files' key. Route it through the shared accessor pair that child 93 defines and exports from scripts/prepareTasks.ts, so a task declaring only the legacy 'files' key is read exactly as if it had declared 'modifiableFiles'. Import that accessor — never re-implement the fallback here, because grouping and preparation diverging is the specific bug this centralisation prevents.
2. Grouping and worktree-scope decisions key off modifiableFiles ONLY. readOnlyFiles must never widen a group or make two tasks collide, even when it is ["*"].

Do NOT edit scripts/prepareTasks.ts (child 93 owns it), scripts/approvalGate.ts, scripts/mergePipeline.ts, any skills/ file, tests/prepareTasks.test.ts, or tests/prepareTasksIntegration.test.ts — those belong to siblings.

Files: scripts/taskGroups.ts, tests/taskGroups.test.ts

Tests: group a task declaring modifiableFiles alongside a legacy task declaring only files, and assert they group identically to the way the legacy pair grouped before the rename. Assert that two tasks whose readOnlyFiles overlap — including when both are ["*"] — do NOT get merged into one group and do not collide, because grouping keys off modifiableFiles only.

Difficulty: 2
description:
Step 4 of the 6-way split of task 58. Scope is scripts/taskGroups.ts and its test. The accessor itself is defined and exported by child 93 from scripts/prepareTasks.ts; this child is the second consumer of it.

Why the accessor is shared rather than duplicated: scripts/prepareTasks.ts declaredFiles (line 100) and scripts/taskGroups.ts declaredFiles (line 16) are two independent readers of the same fence. If they resolve the legacy key differently — even by one edge case, such as an empty array or a task carrying both keys — grouping and preparation disagree about which files a group owns, and a worktree gets scoped to a different set than the brief describes. Routing both through one exported accessor makes that divergence impossible by construction.

Fallback semantics being consumed here: modifiableFiles when present, otherwise the legacy files key. A legacy task must group exactly as it grouped before the rename — this is a pure compatibility requirement, not a behavior change.

Hard invariant this child enforces: grouping and worktree scope key off the modifiable fence ONLY. readOnlyFiles is deliberately allowed to be wide (['*'] means the whole project), so if grouping ever consulted it, every task with a default read fence would collide with every other task and collapse into a single group. The read fence must be invisible to grouping.

Source files are capped at 250 lines — split rather than grow past the cap.

The accessor pair does not exist yet. Task 93 shipped only its part 1; the exported modifiableFiles/readOnlyFiles accessors in scripts/prepareTasks.ts moved to task 154, which is open. This task stays blocked by 154; once it lands, import the accessors under whatever names 154 exports and route scripts/taskGroups.ts's declaredFiles (line 15) through the modifiable accessor, never re-implementing the fallback.

Where the task text names identifiers that do not exist at this base (for example the exported modifiableFiles/readOnlyFiles accessors from task 154's merge), follow the planning prompt's existing rule: plan against what the code holds now and say which names the description got wrong.

Seven scripts read the blockedBy entry key: checkBlockers.ts, blockerVerdicts.ts, unblockDependents.ts, taskStats.ts, runStartup.ts, prepareTasks.ts, and getTaskDetails.ts. The authoring template at skills/create-task/template/taskTemplate.json still documents the old key and must be updated or every new task reintroduces it. No shared TypeScript interface for the entry exists, so there is no single choke point — this is a genuine multi-file mechanical rename.

title: Second codex review only rechecks round-one findings instead of hunting for new ones
userDescription: the codex review prompt needs to indicate that a 2nd review by codex should only verify that the first round's flagged issues were resolved and not try to find new issues.  the purpose is to prevent a runaway review-reject-fix-review-reject-fix loop that happens often.
goal: - On a REJECTED first round, the reviewer's round-one PROBLEMS and FIXES text is written to a file alongside the plan, and that file survives the run so the recheck has something concrete to confirm against.
- Reading skills/tackle-tasks/verify.workflow.js shows the second review runs a distinct recheck prompt — the brief no longer instructs the agent to rerun the identical round-one command.

- The recheck prompt carries the user's proven wording: "check to see if ONLY the issues you flagged in the audit were resolved. Do not look for new issues in the descriptions" — so a plan whose round-one items were fixed comes back APPROVED even when the reviewer could find something else.
- The runaway loop stops reproducing: a task rejected in round one for reasons that were then applied no longer comes back rejected in round two for a brand-new reason.

- NOT in scope: regenerating the brief between review rounds or writing reviewer feedback back into tasks.json. This was investigated with the user and ruled out for the current pipeline — writeTaskBriefFile runs once per plan launch and the verify loop has no separate planner re-write agent. Tasks #83 and #87 in the taskTools-86 chain own that redesign.
- NOT in scope: naming which classes of issue are not grounds for rejection, such as nitpicks and code-fence language tags — task #120 in the taskTools-86 chain owns that lever.
- NOT in scope: the sibling-task and blockedBy scope being added to the same reviewer prompt — task #155 owns that.
- NOT in scope: any test asserting the prompt wording. The user chose no test here because a prompt's instructions change often and such a test would only pin wording.
description: scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexReviewBodyEmitter.ts builds one review prompt, reviewByDefaultPrompt(t), used unchanged by both review rounds; scripts/tackle-tasks/codexReviewsPlan/CODEX_REVIEWS_PLAN.ts calls it through reviewQuestion(t) with no awareness of which round is running. That is the root cause — round two is a fresh full review with no memory of round one, so it is free to reject on problems it never raised before. The fix needs a second prompt, not just changed prose, because prose alone cannot alter what the already-quoted codex exec command asks for. Round one's findings already land in a file next to the plan: t.reviewOutputFile (worktree/plans/codex-review.json) is where codex writes its round-one JSON verdict, and it survives into round two untouched — no new plumbing is needed to persist it, only a second prompt that points the reviewer at it instead of interpolating its contents into a shell command. This repo already carries tests for metacharacter-laden reason strings, so quoting arbitrary reviewer text into a command is a known hazard the file-based approach avoids. Round two must be detected the same way TWO_CODEX_REVIEWS_COMPLETED_Q.ts already does: getAttemptCount(t.number, "planReview", t.taskStateRoot) from scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/taskRunState.ts, made available where CODEX_REVIEWS_PLAN.ts builds the prompt. On round two, reviewQuestion(t) must emit a recheck-only prompt carrying the user's proven wording: "check to see if ONLY the issues you flagged in the audit were resolved. Do not look for new issues in the descriptions" — pointed at t.reviewOutputFile as the audit to recheck against — so a plan whose round-one items were fixed comes back APPROVED even when the reviewer could find something else. The existing two-review cap (TWO_CODEX_REVIEWS_COMPLETED_Q.ts, MAX_ATTEMPTS) and the codex/fable/opus fallback chain in createCodexShellInvocationLive stay as they are; only which prompt reviewQuestion returns changes. Task #155 edits the same reviewer prompt for a different purpose, and groupTasksByFileOverlap will place both in the same worktree group, so no blockedBy is declared. No test pins the recheck prompt's wording — a prompt's instructions change often and such a test would only pin wording; tests stays "skip".

title: Make declaredFiles and addTaskFiles accept modifiableFiles with a fallback to the legacy files key
userDescription: Make the task-file readers accept `modifiableFiles` with a fallback to the legacy `files` key, so the close-tasks migration can be safely re-enabled. This is the missing reader half of task 58's split; task 98 shipped the writer half (the close-tasks migration) but the reader half never landed, so the migration had to be disabled in skills/close-tasks/SKILL.md on 2026-08-08 to stop it blanking every task's file list. Evidence: `declaredFiles(task)` at scripts/taskGroups.ts:15 is the shared accessor and its whole body is `return Array.isArray(task.files) ? (task.files as string[]) : [];` — it reads `files` only. A repo-wide search for `modifiableFiles` across scripts/ returns exactly one hit, a stale comment at scripts/addTaskFiles.ts:6 reading `const FILES_KEY = "files" as const; // repoint here if task 58 splits files into modifiableFiles/readOnlyFiles`. Task 58's children 93-98 are closed, so the split was believed done, but no reader was ever repointed. Required behavior: `declaredFiles` returns `task.modifiableFiles` when present, falls back to `task.files` when not, and returns [] when neither exists; it must never merge the two lists. Add a matching `readOnlyFilesOf(task)` accessor that resolves an absent `readOnlyFiles` to ["*"], since an absent key is meaningful and must stay implicit. Repoint scripts/addTaskFiles.ts's FILES_KEY so appends land on whichever key the task already carries, defaulting to `files` for unmigrated tasks, and drop the stale comment. Every other reader must route through the accessor rather than touching task.files directly. Files: scripts/taskGroups.ts, scripts/addTaskFiles.ts, tests/taskGroups.test.ts, skills/close-tasks/SKILL.md. The SKILL.md edit is the last step: restore the full migration section verbatim from commit 3be16f7, replacing the DISABLED block, only after the readers pass their tests. Tests: fixture tasks holding only `files`, only `modifiableFiles`, both keys, and neither; assert declaredFiles returns the legacy list, the new list, the modifiableFiles list with no merging, and [] respectively; assert readOnlyFilesOf returns ["*"] for a task with no readOnlyFiles key and the declared list otherwise; assert addTaskFiles appends to `modifiableFiles` on a migrated task and to `files` on an unmigrated one. Difficulty 4. This task must land before any close-tasks run is allowed to rename the key.
goal: - `declaredFiles(task)` returns `modifiableFiles` when the task declares it, `files` when it does not, and [] when it declares neither
- a task declaring both keys resolves to `modifiableFiles` alone; the two lists are never merged
- `readOnlyFilesOf(task)` returns ["*"] for a task that declares no `readOnlyFiles`, and the declared list otherwise
- `addTaskFiles` appends to whichever key the task already carries, defaulting to `files` on an unmigrated task
- the stale FILES_KEY comment in scripts/addTaskFiles.ts naming task 58 is gone
- as the last step, the close-tasks migration section is restored verbatim from commit 3be16f7, replacing the DISABLED block
- NOT in scope: renaming any key inside tasks.json. The close-tasks migration step delivered by task 98 owns that, and it stays disabled until this task lands
description:
The reader half of task 58's modifiableFiles/readOnlyFiles split was never built, even though children 93-98 all closed. `declaredFiles` in scripts/taskGroups.ts is the shared accessor every grouping and planning path routes through, and it reads `task.files` only; a repo-wide search finds `modifiableFiles` nowhere in scripts/ except a stale FILES_KEY comment in scripts/addTaskFiles.ts. Task 98 shipped the writer half on 2026-08-08 as a Migration section in skills/close-tasks/SKILL.md, which renames `files` to `modifiableFiles` unconditionally on every close-tasks run. Because no reader accepts the new key, running that migration would make every task's file list resolve to [], silently blinding grouping, planning and split-task. That section was therefore disabled in place the same day, with its full rules preserved in commit 3be16f7 and a pointer left in SKILL.md. This task closes the gap so the migration can be turned back on. The fallback must never merge the two lists — merging would widen an edit fence, which is the exact thing the split exists to keep narrow. An absent `readOnlyFiles` stays absent and resolves to ["*"] at read time rather than being materialised onto the record. Restoring the SKILL.md section is strictly the final step, after the reader tests pass.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

User decision: the userDescription's scope governs — every live direct task.files reader routes through the accessor. The files list now includes those readers (fence checkers, worktree creation, commit, merge, split, clarify) and their existing tests. scripts/tackle-tasks-v1_1_AgentPromptEmitter.ts also reads task.files directly but is frozen v1.1 and stays untouched. The two fence checkers matter most: on a modifiableFiles-only task they would compute an empty owned set and mis-fence the whole worktree.
tests: In tests/taskGroups.test.ts, build four fixture tasks: one declaring only `files`, one declaring only `modifiableFiles`, one declaring both, and one declaring neither. Assert declaredFiles returns the legacy list, the new list, the modifiableFiles list with no merging, and [] respectively. Also assert readOnlyFilesOf returns ["*"] for a task with no readOnlyFiles key and the declared list otherwise, and that addTaskFiles appends to `modifiableFiles` on a migrated task and to `files` on an unmigrated one.

title: Make the Stop hook auto-stage only this session's hunks before asking for a commit message
userDescription: make the hook that produces the 'invoke the commit-message' skill auto-stage only the chunks in this session by keeping a list of files modified during the session, via the hook's payload that provides the transcript path and reading the list of files modified in the transcript path, unless there's an easier way to find out (maybe the hook payload lists files?).
goal: - After the Stop hook runs, `git diff --cached` shows only hunks this session produced; hunks another agent or an earlier session left in the same file stay unstaged.
- A session that modified no files stages nothing and does not ask the agent to invoke the commit-message skill.
- A missing or unreadable per-session flag file makes the hook stage nothing and print why, rather than falling back to staging everything.
- Explicitly NOT in scope: committing. The hook stages and then hands off to the commit-message skill, which the agent still invokes; no task here makes the hook run `git commit`.
description: The Stop/SubagentStop hook `scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts` already reads a per-session file list from `~/.claude/turn-flags/<session_id>`, written by the PostToolUse hook `scripts/turn-modified-flag.ts` from `input.tool_input.file_path`. No transcript parsing is needed — the hook payload already supplies file paths directly, so the user's transcript-reading premise is unnecessary. Today the Stop hook only checks whether those paths are unstaged and emits `additionalContext` telling the agent to stage them itself; it stages nothing. This task makes the hook stage, scoping `git add` per repo or submodule via `dirname(p)` the way the existing porcelain check does. Per-hunk scoping is in scope and is the hard part: `turn-modified-flag.ts` records paths only, not line ranges, so the hook needs either a pre-session content snapshot per file or scripted patch selection to separate this session's hunks from unrelated ones inside the same file. Choosing between those two is the main design decision.
tests: Build a temp repo with 3 dirty files. Write a fake per-session flag file listing only 2 of them. Run the hook. Assert `git diff --cached --name-only` lists exactly those 2. Then extend it: give one of those 2 files both a session hunk and an unrelated pre-existing hunk, and assert only the session hunk appears in `git diff --cached` while the unrelated hunk still shows in `git diff`.

title: 'changes detected' Stop hook prints the real staged diff
userDescription: make the 'changes detected' hook print out what changes are actually staged, because the agent's view of staged changes is always stale.  It should use the same code that the commit-message hook uses to provide the list of staged changes.
goal: - After a turn that edits and stages a file, the Stop hook's additionalContext contains the actual `git diff --staged` text for that file, not only the generic 'Files were changed' sentence.
- The staged-diff text comes from the same scripts/stagedDiffs.ts code path the commit-message skill uses; no second copy of the diff logic exists in the repo.
- The full diff is emitted, not a file-name-only list.
- Staged changes in a submodule whose pointer moved appear in the hook output, labelled per repo, the same way the commit-message skill labels them.
- `npm test` passes, including an updated tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts that asserts the staged-diff text is present in additionalContext.

- NOT in scope: changing the commit-message skill's own output or wording, changing the EXCLUDES list in stagedDiffs.ts, and changing the staging behaviour itself -- the hook still only reports, it never stages.
description:
The 'changes detected' hook is scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts (Stop/SubagentStop), which currently only checks `git status --porcelain` column two per file to decide if anything is unstaged, then emits a generic additionalContext string 'Files were changed. Stage the changes...' with no diff content. The commit-message skill already has the reusable staged-diff code in scripts/stagedDiffs.ts: it resolves the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from `process.cwd()`, runs `git diff --staged` with an EXCLUDES filter, and recurses into any submodule whose pointer moved. Note stagedDiffs.ts is currently a top-level script that writes to stdout, not an exported function -- confirm its actual shape in the source before assuming an export exists; extracting a reusable function is expected. stage-and-summarize-stop.ts must call that shared code and include the actual staged-diff text in the additionalContext payload instead of the generic reminder, so the agent sees what is really staged rather than trusting its stale in-context view. The user chose the FULL staged diff, not a file-name-only list, and chose reuse of the same code over a new lighter implementation. Complication: stage-and-summarize-stop.ts iterates over `paths` that can span multiple repos/submodules (using `dirname(p)` per path), while stagedDiffs.ts resolves only one repo root from cwd with no repo parameter, so this task must either loop the stagedDiffs logic per distinct repo root among the flagged paths, or add a repo-path parameter. tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts's `run()` helper currently asserts additionalContext matches /commit-message skill/ and does not exercise diff content, so the tests need updating to assert the emitted diff text appears in additionalContext.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

scripts/stagedDiffs.ts already exports stagedDiffs() (line 27) with a CLI guard at line 55 — the extraction this description asks to confirm is done. It takes no repo argument and resolves a single root from cwd; the remaining work is the repo-path parameter. 'The hook still only reports, it never stages' means not in scope for this task; task 160 owns staging behavior.
tests: Unit test on the hook: create a temp git repo, write and `git add` a file, feed scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts its Stop-hook JSON on stdin (with a turn-flag file listing that path), and assert the printed hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext contains the staged diff text for that file.

title: Store tasks in SQLite with tags so blockers and files are queries, not agents
userDescription: find a way to store tasks so that they're queryable so that an agent isn't needed to investigate open tasks that block and an agent isn't needed to find the files it touches.  probably needs some kind of tagging system per task/file.
goal: - A query script answers "what blocks task N" and "which open tasks touch file X" from the SQLite database, with no agent run
- A script regenerates a human-readable tasks.json from the database on demand, and the regenerated file matches what the database holds
- /create-task shows the derived tags for approval and accepts user-supplied tags instead
- createTask.workflow.js no longer spawns the blocker-hunter or file-hunter agents; it calls the query script
- The existing test suite still passes: npm test reports no failures after the storage swap
- NOT in scope: the .done file watcher handshake — task 187 owns that
description:
Move task storage from .taskTools/tasks.json to a queryable SQLite database at .taskTools/tasks.db. Use node:sqlite or bun:sqlite — already stdlib, so no new dependency. package.json has no "dependencies" key at all today, only @types/node.

Add per-task and per-file tags so 'what blocks task N' and 'which open tasks touch file X' are SQL queries instead of agent research. The query system should behave like the context-mode query system: structured lookups, not prose. Tags are derived automatically from what a task already has, then presented to the user for approval ("do these tags match? [list]"), with an optional "specify tags" path so the user can supply their own.

Keep a human-readable escape hatch: scripts/generateTasksJson.ts regenerates tasks.json from the database on demand, so a person can still read the task list until the SQLite version is fully integrated everywhere.

Then retire the research agents. skills/create-task/createTask.workflow.js currently spawns two parallel agent() calls through runWithFallback — file-hunter (FILE_HUNTER_SCHEMA: files/description/difficulty) and blocker-hunter (BLOCKER_HUNTER_SCHEMA: blockedBy). Both must be replaced with direct calls to the new query script, and skills/create-task/SKILL.md updated to match.

Existing code to rework: all task I/O funnels through scripts/taskFiles.ts (resolveTaskFiles, readTaskFile, seedTaskFilesIfAbsent) and scripts/appendTask.ts (appendTaskToTasksJson, buildTaskEntry), which read and write tasks.json as a flat JSON array of TaskRecord objects with fields taskNumber, title, userDescription, goal, description, files, tests, difficulty, blockedBy, chainGoal, handoffFilePaths. These become the database-backed read/write layer. scripts/checkBlockers.ts and scripts/getUnblockedTaskNumbers.ts do in-memory graph and cycle detection over blockedBy arrays loaded from tasks.json; that logic becomes SQL. scripts/getTaskDetails.ts, scripts/addTaskFiles.ts, scripts/nextTaskNumber.ts and scripts/closeTasks.ts all read or write tasks.json and must follow.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

'All task I/O funnels through scripts/taskFiles.ts and scripts/appendTask.ts' understates the blast radius: roughly thirty files read tasks.json directly (scripts/prepareTasks.ts, PREAMBLE_STATUS_CHECK.ts via jq, resetTask.ts, taskStats.ts, viewTaskHook.ts, and others). Per this task's own design the regenerated tasks.json stays authoritative for those readers; they are not migrated by this task.
tests: Seed a fixture task set into the database, run the query script for 'which open tasks touch file X' and 'what blocks task N', and assert the answers match hand-checked expected results, with no agent involved.

title: Add a /mermaid skill that diagrams a codebase into a .mmd file
userDescription: make a '/mermaid' skill that searches a codebase and builds a .mmd mermaid diagram.  it should follow the same mermaid diagram rules that I used for the diagrams in taskTools-86 (Yes/No boxes at decision points, output boxes -> what gets outputted, etc)

- Running /mermaid against a codebase writes a .mmd file the user can name and open.

The skill only reads generateSteps.ts as the reference parser whose grammar its output must match; the skill's own output documents an arbitrary codebase and need not itself be runnable by generateSteps.ts.
description:
Add a new /mermaid skill (skills/mermaid/SKILL.md, following the existing skill format seen in skills/view-task/SKILL.md and skills/create-task/SKILL.md) that searches a target codebase and emits a .mmd mermaid flowchart. It must codify the diagramming grammar already used in diagrams/tackle-tasks/*.mmd and parsed by scripts/generateSteps.ts (see getEdgesInDiagram and getPromptBoxesInDiagram, roughly lines 60-120, and the class-role usage around lines 200-210): `flowchart TB`, boxes declared inside a named `subgraph ... end` block as `BOX_ID["label"]` (a decision box is a plain rectangular box whose id ends in `_Q`, not a diamond node), edges written `A -- "label" --> B` or `A --> B`, decision boxes branching with two edges whose labels are literally `YES` and `NO` (extra detail can follow on a `
` line) rather than separate `_YES`/`_NO` boxes, a `classDef`/`class` block at the end assigning every box exactly one role among `script`, `returns_a_prompt`, `next_diagram`, `output`, and `fail`, and any box the diagram references but does not itself resolve grouped into a second `subgraph ... ["next diagram"]` block joined to the main subgraph by an invisible `~~~` link. Reference examples: diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-planTheTask.mmd, diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-whatIsReviewVerdict.mmd, and diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-preambleStatusCheck.mmd. No existing skill in skills/ produces diagrams; this is a new skill directory, not an edit to an existing one. The skill must also carry an explicit written checklist of these diagram rules that it follows while it draws. The /mermaid skill documents codebases generally, not just taskTools pipelines, so its output does not need to be runnable by generateSteps.ts (which is hardcoded to the tackle-tasks box-ownership map) — it only needs to follow the same grammar.
tests: skip -- generateSteps.ts is hardcoded to the tackle-tasks pipeline's box-ownership map (BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER) and its cross-diagram remapping, so it cannot run as a general-purpose grammar validator against a diagram of an arbitrary codebase. Acceptance is checked against the written checklist inside the skill itself (every box declared in a subgraph, every edge label cosmetic, every box assigned a class, decision boxes branch on YES/NO edge labels) rather than a runnable script.

title: Read the diagram folder for tackle-tasks from .taskTools/settings.json
userDescription: The ability to define which set of diagrams to use for tackle-tasks.  this ability makes the skill and pipeline runner generic, allowing the end user to provide their own diagrams.  the default diagram would be the current pipeline.  .taskTools/settings.json is where this diagram setting would live.

- With settings.json holding `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`, generateSteps, the workflow and the hook all read that folder; the run-log names that folder's blocks and none of the default pipeline's.

No .taskTools/settings.json file or reader exists anywhere in the codebase yet (grepped scripts/, skills/, tests/) — this would be a new config file and a new settings-read helper, most naturally added in generateSteps.ts's CLI entrypoint (diagramFolder resolution) ahead of its current argv/hardcoded-default fallback, with the current diagrams/tackle-tasks folder becoming the default when no setting is present.

Setting shape settled with the user: `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`. The folder holds the .mmd files plus each block's script and template. An absent file or key means diagrams/tackle-tasks.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

User decision: both step consumers stay in the fence. scripts/runStepHook.ts and scripts/generateWorkflow.ts are owned so the merge fence cannot block this task, whichever consumer ends up edited. The setting may still flow only through regenerated scripts/steps.json (also owned), in which case the hook and workflow generator need no code change.
